full_judgment:
Kazi Ebadul Hoque J: This Rule was issued at the instance of the Second-party petitioner Abdul Karim calling upon the first party opposite-parties and the State to show cause as to why the judgment and order dated 27-3-97 passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge, 3rd Court, Sylhet allowing Criminal Motion No. 29(iii) of 1995 setting aside the order dated 5-7-1995 passed by the learned Magistrate First Class, Sylhet in Misc. Case No. 91 of 1989 arising out of NGR Case No.156 of 1967 should not be quashed. 

 2. Learned Advocate for the petitioner submitted that learned Magistrate on consideration of the facts and circumstances of the case having rejected the prayer of the first party for delivery of possession of the disputed land learned Additional Sessions Judge acted illegally in setting aside the same under an erroneous conception that report submitted by the police officer of the Kotwali PS was not acceptable. 

 3. It appears from materials on record that the first party has been moving from pillar to post since 1967 in this matter. NGR Case No. 156 of 1967 was started on the application of the 1st party and the disputed land was attached and officer-in-charge of Kotwali PS was appointed receiver of the disputed land in that processing. After considering the evidence learned Magistrate kept the disputed property under attachment in the custody of the receiver under section 146 of the Code of Criminal Procedure by order dated 21-7-69 and directed to get the matter decided by the civil Court. Thereafter, first party filed Title Suit No.286 of 1970 against the second party petitioner and got decree which was upheld upto this Court in CR Case No. 92 of 1989. Thereafter first party filed an application before the learned Magistrate First Class, Sylhet for directing OC Kotwali PS who is the receiver to hand over possession of the attached property to him in pursuance of the decree of the civil Court. But the receiver having submitted a report that second party illegally entered into the disputed land in 1971, learned Magistrate by order dated 10-3-1991 rejected the prayer of the first party. In Criminal Revision No. 29(iii)/1991 filed by the first party the said order was set aside by judgment and order dated 25-4-93 and Magistrate was directed to dispose of the Misc. Case No. 91/1989 on the basis of the evidence adduced by the first party. Thereafter by order dated 5-7-95 learned Magistrate 1st Class again rejected the prayer of the first party. Being aggrieved by the same first party filed Criminal- Motion No. 29(iii) of 1995 and by the impugned judgment and order dated 27-3-97 motion was allowed and order dated 5-7-95 of the learned Magistrate was set aside and the Magistrate was directed to take necessary steps for delivering possession of the disputed land in favour of the first-party Being aggrieved by the same 2nd party petitioner moved this Court and obtained the present Rule. 

 4. It has been held in the case of Jogendra Kumar Dutta vs Noor Mohammad and others reported in 1981 BLD (AD) 248. "Property under attachment under section 145 of the Code of Criminal Procedure is in custodialegis" As soon as the disputed property is attached it comes under the custody of the Court and on behalf of the court the receiver appointed by the Court only manages such property. There is no scope for the receiver to say that the second-party dispossessed him from the attached disputed property. When 'the receiver is a police officer we fail to understand how he could be dispossessed from the disputed property since he has authority to arrest anyone and send him to jail and also prosecute him for committing a congnizable offence or for violating law and order. It is apparent from the conduct of the OC that he is siding with the second-party and raised a frivolous plea to frustrate the decree passed against him and upheld up to this Court and obtained in pursuance of the direction of the learned Magistrate keeping the property under attachment under the provisions of section 146 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for his failure to determine possession of either party on the basis of the evidence adduced before him. In such circumstances the Magistrate is duty bound as the custodian of the disputed property to take over possession of the same from the 2nd party who is bound by the decree of the civil Court and to make over the same to the first-party. In the facts and circumstances of the case we find no illegality in the impugned judgment and order of learned Additional Sessions Judge setting aside the order of the learned Magistrate.
